Afroasiatic languages.subject: World Geography
Afroasiatic languages.question: The _____ was Large language family of Africa and West Asia.
Afroasiatic languages.fact: The Afroasiatic languages (also called the Afro-Asiatic, Afrasian, Hamito-Semitic, or Semito-Hamitic languages) are a language family (or phylum) of about 400 languages spoken predominantly in West Asia, North Africa, the Horn of Africa, and parts of the Sahara and Sahel. The vast majority of Afroasiatic languages are considered indigenous to the African continent, including all those not belonging to the Semitic branch (which originated in West Asia).

Afromontane.subject: World Geography
Afromontane.question: The _____ was Subregion of the Afrotropical realm.
Afromontane.fact: The Afromontane regions are subregions of the Afrotropical realm, one of the Earth's eight biogeographic realms, covering the plant and animal species found in the mountains of Africa and the southern Arabian Peninsula. The Afromontane regions of Africa are discontinuous, separated from each other by lower-lying areas, and are sometimes called the Afromontane archipelago, as their distribution is analogous to a series of sky islands.

Afrophidia.subject: World Geography
Afrophidia.question: The _____ was Clade of snakes comprising large and venomous species.
Afrophidia.fact: Afrophidia is a clade of alethinophidian snakes comprising the groups Henophidia and Caenophidia, essentially making up the snakes people commonly associate with. The name refers to the deep split between Afrophidia and their sister taxon, Amerophidia, which originated in South American origin, and the afrophidians was recently hypothesized to represent a vicariant event of the breakup of Gondwanan South America and Africa.

Afrotropical realm.subject: World Geography
Afrotropical realm.question: What is Afrotropical realm? One of Earth's eight biogeographic realms.
Afrotropical realm.fact: The Afrotropical realm is one of the Earth's eight biogeographic realms.

Afrovenator.subject: World Geography
Afrovenator.question: The _____ was Extinct genus of theropod dinosaurs.
Afrovenator.fact: Afrovenator (; "African hunter") is an extinct genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Middle or Late Jurassic Tiourarén Formation and maybe the Irhazer II Formation of the Sahara region of Niger in western Africa. Afrovenator represents the only named definitive Gondwanan megalosaur, with proposed material of the group present in the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay and the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania, both dated to the Late Jurassic.
